quote_text:
Just listening to your TV interview and the Rio Ngumoha incident,
it turns out you said that he was actually injured?
No, not injured.
He had cramps before that, three minutes where he went to the floor.
And then I had contact with him and he said that it was enough,
so that's why I took him off.
Clearly the booing stood out, and there were boos at the end as well.
- Yeah. - How do you respond to that?
I said it, I think in the same interview:
it makes complete sense if you take a player off who's playing well, who assisted,
that people don't expect you to take that player off,
which wasn't my intention to do.
But he's a good player,
but I don't think he's at the level yet to play at 60% or 50%
to then make the difference.
But maybe, maybe the fans have a different opinion,
they think that he would have been able to play at this level at 50% or 60% -
no matter what the percentage is -
but not being fit enough anymore to sprint and to make your actions.
So, yeah, if you don't know that then you feel like,
"Why is he taking him off?"
Then I understand that reaction.
I knew the moment his number went up that that would have been the reaction.
But that's not a reason then not to do it and keep a player in the team
who tells me he cannot continue.
And after the game. I think it also makes sense,
because I don't think this club should be happy with a 1-1 result against Chelsea.
We always aim for a win, and if we don't win, then we're disappointed.
And especially in a season where we haven't won a lot,
or not as much as people expect us to do, then it's just building up frustration.
And that came out probably after half-time, but I think the players and myself
had the same frustration as the fans.
Arne, you got off to a dream start with the early goal.
It felt like then you seemed to back off and slow the game down
against a team that are obviously so vulnerable with the form they're in.
Is that what you told them to do?
Yeah, I said after we scored the 1-0 and then we got a big chance for the 2-0,
didn't you see me screaming off the sideline, "Go back, go back!
"Defend your own box, defend your own box!"
Are you really thinking this is serious...
Of course it's not the idea for us to back off.
We wanted to keep going,
but we played against a team that got more and more comfortable on the ball,
they didn't have any wingers available, so they had a lot of midfielders,
so they controlled the midfield and started to play,
passing through us more and more and more.
Which didn't lead to a lot of chances,
but they were by far the dominant team in the game.
And it was difficult to change that during the first half.
But I think you might have noticed as well, apart from other things you've noticed,
that at half-time we changed things.
That didn't lead straightaway to what we wanted,
because three minutes afterwards we conceded the 2-1,
which was - good for us - fractionally offside.
But then afterwards, we were much more able to press them high,
to keep them in their half.
Not perfect, because they were still a few times able to play through us,
but not as much as in the first half.
So, that was the adjustment we made at half-time
which helped us being the more dominant team in the second half -
but not able to score. We were twice close.
But I think it's not fair to me,
that anyone could ever think that I tell my players to back off
and to drop down and not to press.
Then either you haven't seen my teams playing last season,
and a large part of this season, let alone since I'm a manager.
It did look like that, that we drop down,
but that is never the intention.
That was, in this situation, us not being able to control all the midfielders.
Arne, I'm wondering, you mentioned the frustrations from yourself and the players,
Ryan Gravenberch after the game said he felt the boos were quite justified.
I'm just wondering, those frustrations, are they starting to become a bit of a problem?
Yes, because usually frustrations come from losing more than we want.
And losing more than we want is never a good thing, that's always a problem.
So, yeah, it's not ideal, but I think I felt the support
towards the players throughout the whole game.
Of course there were moments where they showed
that they would love to see something else, but they weren't the only ones.
I'm 100% sure the players on the pitch would have shown a different face,
and me on the side would have loved us to show a different face as well.
But sometimes - and we're not the only team -
sometimes you play against teams that can have a certain spell in the game as well,
a good spell in the game,
and then you have to defend, which I think we did,
because in that part they didn't create a lot of chances.
But, as [has happened] so many times this season, as last week,
we conceded a set-piece.
And that made the difference in not only not feeling nice
that we were not controlling the game, but even add the set-piece to that.
And then of course it's very negative.
But the second half was different from our side.
Similar in the first 10 minutes maybe.
But I think also one of our problems is that
when we ARE the better team, we are not able to score.
And so it's not only the spell where the other team is better
that we then concede.
Maybe it's a bigger problem,
that if we are the better team on the pitch, we are not able to find the second goal.
The good thing between now and last week is that,
last week, when we were the better team on the pitch, we conceded a goal,
and now at least we got a draw - which we are not happy with, let that be clear.
Do you know what Ibrahima Konate's problem was?
He seemed to be limping off.
And would you expect anyone else back for Villa on Friday?
Eh, Konate... Yeah, we always have to wait and see.
The way he limped off...
He told me it was cramp,
but, yeah, let's hope he's right in his assessment.
But, yeah, we have to wait and see tomorrow how he feels and how that will work out.
I think Mo [Salah] is close to returning, Ali is close to returning
With Flo [Wirtz] we have to wait and see how he's recovering, with what he has.
Do we have other players that might come back?
No, I don't think so.
There's obviously a bit of a difference between fans online and in the stadium,
it feels like the stadium are starting to show their frustration,
and it could be a bit harder to convince them.
Do you still feel confident that you can get all of those fans back in time?
Yeah, I do.
Not this season, by the way.
This season they will have their opinion and it will not change.
But if we can have the summer that we are planning to have,
then I'm 100% convinced that we will be a different team next season than we are now.
Different in terms of results, different in how things look.
But it's not always that simple,
because sometimes you know what you have to do,
but it's not always possible to also get exactly what you want.
But for us, for me, it's really clear what we are lacking this season.
And we're trying with the players we're having now -
because one of the things we are lacking is players that are fit!
But the players that we have available now, I think again,
like last week, like this week,
showed in the second half that they want to give everything and try to push.
But it was not enough last week and wasn't enough this week
to find that goal which we maybe deserved,
if you looked at where the game was played,
because for me the game was mainly played, in the second half, in their half.
And that that is what we've seen a lot of times this season,
but we've also seen a lot of times this season that being the dominant team
doesn't lead to chance after chance after chance.
Just on that point,
there have been a lot of frustrating home games this season.
Away games as well, but also home games.
Particularly in terms of winning the fans back...
How important is that going into next season,
that you somehow wrestle back control of those games
and manage to impose your will on the opposition?
I think it's so simple.
What the fans want to see, what I want to see, what everyone wants to see,
is a team that creates chances from ball possession.
And that's what we are not doing enough.
If you simply look at the difference
between the goals scored last season and this season, it is an enormous gap.
The goals conceded is not so much difference between this and last season.
But the goals scored is the biggest difference between this and last season.
And I think if the same fans see a similar type of game
but then it leads to more chances,
they would be much more happy with what they are seeing -
first of all because they see more chances.
Usually when you get more chances you score more, and that leads to a win.
And we all know, I know now, from being so long in football,
that judging a performance is mainly also done by results.
And...
And maybe last season I think we played a quite similar game against Chelsea,
but the difference was, last season, we found many times a way to score a goal,
which we are struggling with this season.
And that's just when you look at our goal-scoring,
the goal-scorers this season and you compare it to last season.
Yeah, that's a massive difference.
Just on the boos, it's happened probably three or four times.
How does that make you feel?
And also this idea of, if it happens once, it's a one-off,
but it's becoming a pattern now.
What is the English word for that? It sometimes feels...
How do I find the right word?
No, let me describe it in a different way.
I would love to show them something else.
But at this moment of time, we're not enough able to.
What we are able to do is to be the dominant team,
to have, more than the other team, the ball,
as has happened so many times this season.
And I want to give them much more to be positive about or happy about.
And I am 100 sure the team wants that the same.
But as I said many times now, ball possession is one thing,
but to generate chances from that...
Second half last week, everybody was probably really positive about our second half,
but from open play we did not create one chance.
And then we scored two goals and everybody's much more positive.
But we had 60 per cent possession at Old Trafford,
which, apart from City, who had a bit more ball possession than us...
But it's not my idea to like ball possession -
I like to create chances.
I like to create and score goals.
And I know what we need to get that done.
And I think this club, last season and all the season before,
can show all of you what you need to bring ball possession to chances.
Because that has happened so many times here,
what you need for that, and we haven't produced that enough this season.
title: Konate Update, Ngumoha & Performance  | Press Conference | Liverpool 1-1 Chelsea
